title: Scenario Playflows — Rapid Iteration Deck (draft)
content:
Purpose: rapid, scenario-driven slide pack + speaker notes for AE/SE to handle multi-turn sales conversations. The goal is to give concise flows (1–2 slides each) that can be stitched together in calls. This is a working draft — lots of TODOs and example scripts below.

Audience: Sales Engineers, AEs running discovery & proof-of-concept calls. Primary use: 10–25 minute call segments, demo transitions, handling model/perf/cost objections quickly.

High-level structure (slide-by-slide suggestions):
1) Title slide (1): Scenario name + quick TL;DR (30–45s). Keep header: Scenario + one-sentence outcome.

2) Executive hook (1): Why this matters to the buyer. Script snippet: "Most teams we speak to need predictable latency and unit economics more than absolute SOTA — we optimize for both. Quick example: X tokens/day -> Y cost savings with caching/quantization."

3) Persona & Pain (1): Customer persona (e.g., mid-market CRM platform, fraud ops team, enterprise search) + top pain (throughput, variance in latency, isolation/compliance). Quick bullet list; include one measurable success metric (OPS: reduce 95p latency by 30% or cut inference cost per 1M tokens by 40%).

4) Recommended model+deployment pattern (1): Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private decision tree (2–3 bullets):
   - Hosted: fastest onboarding, good for smaller volumes and prototyping. mention credits/free tier.
   - Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for steady high-throughput with SLAs.
   - Private: VPC/on-prem for regulated data.
   Speaker note: always ask about data residency + compliance first.

5) Quick demo flow (2): Step 1 demo – show prompt -> result; Step 2: show how to change batching/cache profile and immediate effect.
   - Key metric to surface live: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens.

6) Objection playflows (4–6 micro-slides): Each micro-slide = objection, one-paragraph reframing, demo action, rebuttal script, fallback. Examples below. Keep each to 3 bullets.

7) Comparison snippet (1): concise competitor callouts (friendly tone).
   - Focus on practical delta: unified routing + graceful fallbacks + per-token cost visibility. Avoid deep feature bragging — call out where customers care (ops + finance).

8) Pricing signal + ROI calc (1): back-of-envelope calc for 3 workload archetypes (low, medium, high). show numbers, not percentages.

9) Close + next steps (1): CTA: run a 2-week proof with sample dataset, or schedule platform deep-dive with infra + sec.

Slide content examples / speaker notes (copyable):
- Hook script: "If you care about keeping latency predictable during traffic spikes, there are two levers we'd take right away: (1) localized KV prefix caching for hot prompts, (2) fallbacks to a smaller quantized variant when tail latency spikes. We can show both on a short PoC."

- Discovery questions (ask early):
  1) What are your 95p and 99p latency SLOs?
  2) Typical tokens per request and concurrency?
  3) Any regulatory constraints or data residency needs?
  4) Do you have strict cost targets per 1k responses?

- Objection: "We run everything on our infra / can't move data."
  - Reframe: We offer Private deployments (VPC + optional on-prem) with the same API, minimizing code changes.
  - Demo action: show sample config (pin model version + routing policy) and highlight audit logs.
  - Script: "We can run the exact same calls you already make via an endpoint in your VPC; the code change is just the endpoint URL and credentials."

- Objection: "Your hosted pricing is too unpredictable."
  - Reframe: Walk through dedicated options and our Optimize recommendations (quantization + batching). Pull up sample ROI table (quick math).
  - Script: "We can run an analysis on your historical traces and produce a projected monthly invoice with variance bands."

- Objection: "We need SSO + stricter audit logs."
  - Reframe: point to Private offering + KMS/HSM integrations + structured audit event format.
  - Script: "We map to your current SIEM and can provide export hooks for 12+ months of logs."

Demo playtips (for SEs):
- Keep sample prompts short and repeatable. Use a fixed seed when showing nondeterministic models.
- Show metric differences after toggling one setting (e.g., enable batching -> show tokens/sec increase).
- Have a prepared fallback endpoint (smaller quantized model) to flip during live calls if latency spikes.

Short checklist for call prep (copyable):
- [ ] Confirm attendee roles (is auditor in call?)
- [ ] Bring dataset sample (5–10 example prompts)
- [ ] Pre-upload config snippet for private demo if needed (VPC details)
- [ ] Run a smoke test in demo environment 10 min before call

Open items / TODOs:
- Add 2 vertical-specific slides for: Insurance claims automation + E-commerce search (Priya to draft)
- Add short competitor language for low-latency inference providers (Diego)
- Create 1-pager ROI sheet per archetype (Connor)
- Clean up pricing calc numbers and attach spreadsheet (link placeholder: sheets://roi-archetypes)

Notes to self (rough):
- Avoid using the word "best" vs competitors — use measurable deltas.
- Keep the deck modular: micro-slides should be copy/paste-able into customer-specific decks.
- We should A/B test two variants of the objection script: empathetic vs technical. Track conversion after 6 weeks.

Appendix: quick numbers to cite (internal):
- Typical p95 improvement after KV caching: 15–40% (varies by workload)
- Cost reduction with 4-bit quantization on Llama-like models: 20–50% (dependent on perf/regression tolerance)
- Example ROI: 12M tokens/day -> projected infra cost reduction ~$2,800/month with batching + cache (back-of-envelope).

References & links for follow-up: Confluence (Scenario Playflows Library), Jira GROWTH tickets for sample datasets, PR for updated demo scripts (linked above).

Draft author notes: keep iterations fast. This file is intentionally terse — prioritize building a library of 20 micro-slides (each 1 idea).
